evals.prompt: I'm training a text classification model using scikit-learn. I want to compare TF-IDF + Logistic Regression vs TF-IDF + Random Forest vs sentence-transformers + XGBoost. Set up experiment tracking so I can compare them properly.
evals.expected_output: Should set up MLflow or W&B tracking, define what to log for each run, ensure all three experiments are comparable, and provide the tracking code.
assertions: Sets up experiment tracking infrastructure (MLflow or W&B)
Defines consistent metrics across all three approaches
Logs hyperparameters, dataset version, and git commit for each run
Logs model artifacts for later loading
Shows how to compare runs after completion
Emphasizes changing one variable at a time where possible
Includes reproducibility measures (random seed, environment capture)

evals.prompt: I've been training models in Jupyter notebooks for 3 months and I have results scattered across 40+ notebooks. How do I get organized?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend setting up tracking infrastructure, then systematically re-running or cataloging key experiments. Should be practical about not re-running everything.
assertions: Does NOT suggest re-running all 40 notebooks
Recommends setting up tracking for all future experiments
Suggests cataloging the best results from notebooks into the tracker manually
Recommends extracting reusable training code from notebooks into scripts
Suggests data versioning to prevent future dataset ambiguity
Provides a practical migration path, not an all-or-nothing approach

evals.prompt: Before I wire up MLflow — I don't actually know how to tell whether our RAG support chatbot is answering well. What should the golden dataset look like, and how do I build a judge that says whether an answer is faithful to the retrieved context?
evals.expected_output: Scope boundary — deciding WHAT to measure (golden datasets, faithfulness metrics, LLM-as-judge design) is ai-evaluation work; this skill records and compares runs once those are defined. Should hand off rather than answering with run-logging setup.
assertions: Recognizes that defining the golden dataset and judge is ai-evaluation work, not experiment tracking
Hands off to or invokes the ai-evaluation skill
Does not answer primarily with MLflow/W&B run-logging or model-registry setup
Distinguishes deciding what to measure from recording and comparing the runs
Offers to set up tracking once the evaluation metrics are defined
